## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：cai-2024-1wt-nadfp、che-2021-0.8m-pc-emc。

### 候选资料：che-2021-0.8m-pc-emc（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：PC, EMC；溶剂比例（体积）：PC=1.0, EMC=1.0；添加剂：FEC；添加剂用量：FEC=2 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child1]：Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

### 候选资料：cai-2024-1wt-nadfp（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP；添加剂用量：NaDFP=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4]：2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

## 候选评估
### che-2021-0.8m-pc-emc
评估建议：The candidate (0.8 M NaPF6, PC/EMC 1:1 v/v, 2 wt% FEC) matches the paper's PC/EMC pouch-cell electrolyte, which has directly reported -30 C capacity retention in NFM/HC pouch cells, supporting it as the recommended electrolyte for the -30 C program; no separate computed prediction is available, and the exact 0.8 M vs 1 M attribution of the -30 C figure should be confirmed against Fig. S5.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Target system must be a sodium-ion pouch cell：The paper explicitly evaluates Ah-level NFM/HC sodium-ion pouch cells with these carbonate electrolytes, matching the pouch-cell program context. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec2::child0][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child5]
- Salt must be NaPF6：The study uses NaPF6 as the solute throughout the PC/EMC electrolyte work. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child0][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec2::child0]
- Salt concentration must be 0.8 mol/L：The paper reports 0.8 M NaPF6 electrolytes as the studied concentration in the PC/EMC system. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child1][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8]
- Solvent system must be PC/EMC：The work selects PC/EMC as the base solvent system for the optimized electrolyte. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child0][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec9::child0]
- PC/EMC ratio of 1:1 by volume：The paper uses PC/EMC (1/1, v/v) as the baseline this study builds on; note that the later five-electrolyte comparison used a 2:3 cyclic/linear ratio, so the 1:1 base and the comparison set are not identical formulations. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child0][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child1]
- FEC additive at 2 wt%：The paper states the five 0.8 M NaPF6 electrolytes were prepared using 2 wt% FEC additive, matching the candidate's additive package. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child1]
- Quantified capacity retention relative to room temperature at -30 C：Low-temperature retention for the PC/EMC pouch cell is reported (72.7% at -30 C in one passage; 74.40% at -30 C quoted for the 1 M PC/EMC cell, with 0.8 M noted as slightly lower), which directly addresses the -30 C retention observable; exact attribution between 0.8 M/1 M formulations should be checked against Fig. S5. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child4][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child5]
文献与候选的关联：In this study the NaPF6/carbonate electrolytes were applied to NFM/HC pouch cells, and low-temperature capacity retention was measured on those same pouch cells: the PC/EMC electrolyte cell retained 72.7% at -30 C (with a 1 M PC/EMC cell reported at 74.40% at -30 C), so the composition and the -30 C retention observable are experimentally associated in the same pouch-cell system rather than inferred across systems. [0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child4][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child5][0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec8::child1]

## 下一步核查与验证
- 在目标软包电芯（NFM/HC 或项目实际正负极对）上以 0.5C/1C 放电测 -30 °C 相对 25 °C 容量的保持率，作为主观测量的端到端验证；文献已给出 PC/EMC 体系 72.7%（0.8 M 筛选体系）与 74.40%（1 M 体系）两种实测值，需在项目电芯上复核。
- 确认 Che 2021 中 0.8 M NaPF6 / PC-EMC 所用“第二代添加剂”的完整清单与用量（原文仅在结论中提及），因为 -30 °C 保持率结论绑定在该完整配方上。
- 对 0.8 M NaPF6 + 1 wt% NaDFP / EC:EMC (3:7) 体系补测相对 25 °C 容量的 -30 °C 放电保持率；文献仅以 688 mAh（1C）与基线 459 mAh 报告，缺少室温基准容量。
- 对 TMSS（3 wt%）与 TMSBS（1 wt%）体系补取同批电芯的 25 °C 放电容量，以把已报告的 -30 °C 放电容量（793 mAh / 814 mAh @0.5C）换算为相对室温容量的保持率。
- 补取 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL 的 G2:DOL 比例，并区分“-30 °C 循环保持率”与“-30 °C 相对室温容量保持率”两项不同指标。
- 在近似与目标工况下评估安全性/产气与成本：本项目未提供价格数据，文献仅给出低成本动机，不得据此宣称已验证低成本。

source_refs.raw_quote: Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

source_refs.raw_quote: This was attributed to their low coulombic efficiency and high polarization. Nevertheless, the utilisation of a 3 wt% TMSS electrolyte has been observed to exert a beneficial effect, with the capacity remaining at 80% after 80 cycles. Fig. S11 illustrates the $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle curves. In the initial cycle, batteries with and without TMSS exhibited comparable charge and discharge starting points, approximately 2.4 V and 3.6 V, respectively. However, as the number of cycles increased, the battery without TMSS exhibited a progressively more severe polarization, with only a portion of its capacity retained after 40 cycles. It is noteworthy that the capacity difference between batteries with additives is considerably greater at low temperatures than at room temperature. Meanwhile, at a temperature of $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ , the electrolyte containing TMSS also demonstrated superior rate performance in comparison to the Baseline electrolyte, which is consistent with the results obtained at room temperature (Fig. S12). To further evaluate the battery performance under extreme conditions, a low-temperature discharge test was conducted at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ . As illustrated in Fig. 3d and Fig. S13, batteries with TMSS demonstrated remarkable capacity retention and recovery rates, maintaining 900 mAh, 827 mAh, and 793 mAh under conditions of 0.1C, 0.3C, and 0.5C, while batteries without TMSS only maintained 841 mAh, 705 mAh, and 691 mAh.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a. source_refs.raw_quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. source_refs.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
source_refs.paper_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries
source_refs.raw_quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

source_refs.raw_quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

source_refs.raw_quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, NaDFP is introduced as a dual-functional additive for pouch SIBs to achieve high electrochemical performance within a wide temperature range ( $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). There are two ways to improve the battery performance for NaDFP: i) induce high-quality CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces; ii) optimize the solvation structure to decrease the desolvation energy and surface impendence. Consequently, its role in other types of commercial electrolytes was further investigated. NaDFP electrolyte demonstrates the potential application in wide temperature SIBs from $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Importantly, only 1 wt% addition of NaDFP into electrolyte can enable considerably effective improvement, which is essential to reduce the cost of batteries. Therefore, this work provides a new idea for the optimum design of electrolytes of SIBs and other energy storage equipment.

citations.chunk_id: 0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

association_citations.quote: Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

citations.chunk_id: 0005_Che 等 - 2021 - Engineering optimization approach of nonaqueous electrolyte for sodium ion battery with long cycle l::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec2::child0
citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote: Stable discharge can be achieved at low-temperature rate, reflecting low-temperature adaptability. Fig. 3(a) shows the capacity stabilization effect of TMSBS on the electrolyte at different rates at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . TMSBS electrolyte maintains stable performance under $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ cycling, while the Baseline electrolyte exhibits rapid decay (Fig. S7b). Besides, The extreme low-temperature discharge experiment at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 3b) showed that the cells with TMSBS electrolyte had a capacity of 879, 853, and $814\mathrm{mAh}$ at 0.2, 0.3, and $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), while the cells with Baseline electrolyte had a capacity of 801, 752, and $716\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively (Fig. 3c). In other words, at low temperatures, TMSBS can provide higher electrolyte energy density and achieve greater capacity retention, making it suitable for emergency powering of energy storage devices in extremely cold conditions. The rate performance of SIBs at room temperature is crucial for evaluating their performance in practical applications. High-rate-performance batteries can rapidly charge and discharge in a short period of time, which is particularly important for devices that require high power output, such as electric vehicles and mobile devices [23,36].

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: In summary, NaDFP is introduced as a dual-functional additive for pouch SIBs to achieve high electrochemical performance within a wide temperature range ( $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). There are two ways to improve the battery performance for NaDFP: i) induce high-quality CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces; ii) optimize the solvation structure to decrease the desolvation energy and surface impendence. Consequently, its role in other types of commercial electrolytes was further investigated. NaDFP electrolyte demonstrates the potential application in wide temperature SIBs from $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Importantly, only 1 wt% addition of NaDFP into electrolyte can enable considerably effective improvement, which is essential to reduce the cost of batteries. Therefore, this work provides a new idea for the optimum design of electrolytes of SIBs and other energy storage equipment.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

Because it is easily oxidized on the cathode during the cycling, especially under high voltage or high temperature, which oxidates the lattice oxygen on the surface of the cathode material to produce active $\left(\mathrm{O}_{2}\right)$ species that attacked the solvent molecules, thus resulting in the loss of lattice oxygen and the consumption of the electrolyte [18]. Continuous lattice oxygen loss can lead to an irreversible phase transformation. High temperature cycling and high voltage cycling were followed to confirm the function of the cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) induced by NaDFP. As shown in the Fig. 4a and 4b, the cycling stability and rate performance at 45 °C were improved. As a recent upstart in the field of energy storage, the energy storage efficiency of SIBs under high temperature conditions is one of the main research focuses.

evidence_ledger.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. evidence_ledger.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote: Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

citations.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0
citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

Nevertheless, the utilisation of a 3 wt% TMSS electrolyte has been observed to exert a beneficial effect, with the capacity remaining at 80% after 80 cycles. Fig. S11 illustrates the $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle curves. In the initial cycle, batteries with and without TMSS exhibited comparable charge and discharge starting points, approximately 2.4 V and 3.6 V, respectively. However, as the number of cycles increased, the battery without TMSS exhibited a progressively more severe polarization, with only a portion of its capacity retained after 40 cycles. It is noteworthy that the capacity difference between batteries with additives is considerably greater at low temperatures than at room temperature. Meanwhile, at a temperature of $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ , the electrolyte containing TMSS also demonstrated superior rate performance in comparison to the Baseline electrolyte, which is consistent with the results obtained at room temperature (Fig. S12). To further evaluate the battery performance under extreme conditions, a low-temperature discharge test was conducted at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ . As illustrated in Fig. 3d and Fig. S13, batteries with TMSS demonstrated remarkable capacity retention and recovery rates, maintaining 900 mAh, 827 mAh, and 793 mAh under conditions of 0.1C, 0.3C, and 0.5C, while batteries without TMSS only maintained 841 mAh, 705 mAh, and 691 mAh.

citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec2::child0
citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote:
2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: In summary, NaDFP is introduced as a dual-functional additive for pouch SIBs to achieve high electrochemical performance within a wide temperature range ( $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). There are two ways to improve the battery performance for NaDFP: i) induce high-quality CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces; ii) optimize the solvation structure to decrease the desolvation energy and surface impendence. Consequently, its role in other types of commercial electrolytes was further investigated. NaDFP electrolyte demonstrates the potential application in wide temperature SIBs from $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Importantly, only 1 wt% addition of NaDFP into electrolyte can enable considerably effective improvement, which is essential to reduce the cost of batteries. Therefore, this work provides a new idea for the optimum design of electrolytes of SIBs and other energy storage equipment.

citations.quote: In this work, inspired by lithium difluorophosphate as a dual-functional electrolyte additive of LIBs, NaDFP has a similar structure to lithium difluorophosphate and thus was evaluated as a dual-functional electrolyte additive for NFM/HC pouch SIBs $[9]$ . association_citations.quote:
2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

Nevertheless, the utilisation of a 3 wt% TMSS electrolyte has been observed to exert a beneficial effect, with the capacity remaining at 80% after 80 cycles. Fig. S11 illustrates the $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle curves. In the initial cycle, batteries with and without TMSS exhibited comparable charge and discharge starting points, approximately 2.4 V and 3.6 V, respectively. However, as the number of cycles increased, the battery without TMSS exhibited a progressively more severe polarization, with only a portion of its capacity retained after 40 cycles. It is noteworthy that the capacity difference between batteries with additives is considerably greater at low temperatures than at room temperature. Meanwhile, at a temperature of $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ , the electrolyte containing TMSS also demonstrated superior rate performance in comparison to the Baseline electrolyte, which is consistent with the results obtained at room temperature (Fig. S12). To further evaluate the battery performance under extreme conditions, a low-temperature discharge test was conducted at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ . As illustrated in Fig. 3d and Fig. S13, batteries with TMSS demonstrated remarkable capacity retention and recovery rates, maintaining 900 mAh, 827 mAh, and 793 mAh under conditions of 0.1C, 0.3C, and 0.5C, while batteries without TMSS only maintained 841 mAh, 705 mAh, and 691 mAh.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec2::child0
citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote:
2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: In summary, NaDFP is introduced as a dual-functional additive for pouch SIBs to achieve high electrochemical performance within a wide temperature range ( $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). There are two ways to improve the battery performance for NaDFP: i) induce high-quality CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces; ii) optimize the solvation structure to decrease the desolvation energy and surface impendence. Consequently, its role in other types of commercial electrolytes was further investigated. NaDFP electrolyte demonstrates the potential application in wide temperature SIBs from $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Importantly, only 1 wt% addition of NaDFP into electrolyte can enable considerably effective improvement, which is essential to reduce the cost of batteries. Therefore, this work provides a new idea for the optimum design of electrolytes of SIBs and other energy storage equipment.
